title: Mallow Leaves Stuffed with Brown Rice
subtitle: with greens and tomatoes
description: Foraged mallow leaves (or chard or beet leaves) rolled around a herby brown rice and tomato filling and simmered in lemon, olive oil and pomegranate molasses.

steps.text: Bring plenty of water to the boil in a large pot and prepare a large bowl of iced water. Blanch the mallow leaves in the boiling water for 10 seconds and move them to the iced water.

Put the brown rice, 4 grated tomatoes, chopped herbs, salt, pepper and baharat in a pot. Pour in 0.25 cup olive oil generously and water to cover and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed. The rice should not be cooked through, only release a little starch so it is stickier. Let cool.
Line the base of a 30 cm pot or pan with thin tomato slices (the remaining 2 tomatoes).

Lay each leaf rough side down. Place a spoonful of filling in the centre, leaving about 2 cm at each side, fold the edges over the filling and roll into a tight cigar shape. Arrange the rolls in one layer in the pot with the seam side down.

Pour over the lemon juice, the remaining 0.5 cup olive oil, the pomegranate molasses and water to cover. Place a plate on top as a weight, bring to the boil, lower the heat and cook over low heat for 1.5 hours.
